prior_works.title: Search-R1
prior_works.relationship_sentence: Search-R1 introduced the free-form query-generation RL search-agent paradigm and the final-answer outcome training whose many-to-one query→retrieval mapping is the precise interface Harness-G reforms into a finite action menu.

prior_works.title: Graph-R1
prior_works.relationship_sentence: Graph-R1 brought interactive RL to graph-structured corpora but retained free-form queries over that graph, making it the closest competing system whose retained query interface Harness-G directly replaces with menu selection.

prior_works.title: Tree-GRPO
prior_works.relationship_sentence: Tree-GRPO created finer step-level contrast via tree/anchor grouping but operated on free-query actions, exposing that denser credit alone cannot overcome retrieval aliasing and motivating a structural remedy of the action interface.

prior_works.title: MINERVA
prior_works.relationship_sentence: MINERVA demonstrated discrete, RL-driven navigation over knowledge-graph entities and relations—an explicit finite action formulation that inspired Harness-G's recasting of open-text multihop retrieval as select/lookup/answer choices.

prior_works.title: GraphRAG
prior_works.relationship_sentence: GraphRAG developed programmatic corpus graph representations and provenance-aware retrieval for multi-hop QA, providing the graph-structured evidence space and provenance edges that Harness-G adapts into an online action menu and enablement-credit paths.

prior_works.title: GRPO (Group-Relative Policy Optimization)
prior_works.relationship_sentence: GRPO formalized within-input trajectory grouping and group-relative advantage estimation, forming the optimization machinery Harness-G builds upon and extends with frontier-relative comparisons and enablement propagation in SNC.

synthesis_narrative: Prior work established three complementary technical threads. First, free-query RL search agents such as "Search-R1" and interactive graph-based agents like "Graph-R1" operationalized training LLMs to generate natural-language queries and optimize multi-turn retrieval with outcome rewards, thereby defining the default policy–environment interface and the many-to-one query→retrieval mapping. Second, methods for finer credit (e.g., "Tree-GRPO") and group-relative optimization ("GRPO") developed trajectory grouping and step-contrast machinery to combat sparse final rewards, highlighting algorithmic credit techniques but still operating on the same aliased query actions. Third, discrete navigation and graph retrieval work—exemplified by "MINERVA" for KG path navigation and corpus-graph systems like "GraphRAG"—showed that finite, verifiable action sets and programmatic evidence graphs enable transparent state transitions and provenance wiring for downstream credit. Taken together, these strands reveal a gap: denser credit alone cannot fix structural aliasing in the action interface. This combination naturally suggests converting free-form queries into explicit, bounded menu choices over a paragraph–sentence–entity graph and then exploiting the resulting same-state frontier to compute local contrasts and delayed enablement signals. Harness-G thus synthesizes the graph-based evidence foundation and discrete-action inspiration with GRPO-style grouping, replacing aliased query actions with finite Select/Lookup/Answer choices and introducing Structured Non-myopic Credit (SNC) to compare and retroactively reward retrieval-enabling steps—making the interface design itself a lever for more effective retrieval credit assignment.
